svg.text: GuangzhouLandmarks — Cross-Building Audit and Tuning
2026-09-18 • all seven building Blueprints inspected • 214 Nanite meshes normalised • Guidemen V5 4K detail pass
Two component architectures covered: HISM-based (V5, Zhengnanmen HighFidelity) and StaticMeshComponent-based (the three V3 builds)
Audit — what was inspected
Zhengnanmen_HighFidelity 114 HISM 12,383 inst
Xiaobeimen_AAA_V3 51 SMC 51 inst
Xiaobeimen_Production_V3 16 SMC 16 inst
Zhengnanmen_AAA_V3 25 SMC 25 inst
Guidemen_V5_4K 47 HISM 18,822 inst
Wuxianmen_V5_4K_Core 7 HISM 5,103 inst
Wuxianmen_V5_FullPBR 7 HISM 5,103 inst
Checks applied to every building
roof orientation · elongated-instance outliers · role/mesh name
agreement · Nanite state · custom-data width · materials
The first pass only understood HISM components, so the three V3
builds reported zero; the second pass covers both architectures.
No Wuxianmen-class geometry defects
Roof orientation
Zhengnanmen HighFidelity: centre 374 cm above the perimeter —
rises to a ridge. Guidemen: verified directly from its tile surface,
2,002 cm at the centre falling to 1,465 cm at the perimeter.
Ridge axis
Guidemen's two main ridges run 31.2 m and 27.2 m along X, matching
its pavilion width. No mis-axed bar anywhere.
Two false positives, run down and dismissed
A 2,230 cm "elongated outlier" on Zhengnanmen is the 22.3 m top
rail of its balustrade, running along the building's long axis.
Guidemen's "inverted" verdict came from its 11 large shell
instances; the direct tile profile shows a correct ridge.
The real defect: Nanite fallbacks
214 meshes across five buildings
Guidemen: every one of its 47 meshes, including the 16,248-instance
roof tiles, both roof shells and both main ridges.
Both Xiaobeimen builds and Zhengnanmen AAA V3: roof tiles, roof
shells, ridge ornaments, plaques, doors, railings.
Zhengnanmen HighFidelity: 103 meshes — beams, doors, floor cores,
arch fills, rails, ridge ends, dressed stone, tiles.
Why it matters here
The archive records this editor rendering with Nanite DISABLED on
an SM5 fallback path. On that path the fallback mesh is what draws.
before: error 1.0 percent 1.0 → 1% of triangles
A 53,238-triangle tiled roof would have fallen back to ~532.
Fix 1 — Nanite fallback normalised
Target rule: every Nanite mesh whose fallback is not full-detail, discovered by
scanning the Blueprints rather than an earlier report. That mattered: the report
flagged only error > 0 and missed 103 Zhengnanmen meshes that already had
error 0.0 but percent 1.0 — a partial fix the validation caught.
fallback_relative_error 1.0 → 0.0
fallback_percent_triangles 1.0 → 100.0
Applied through StaticMeshEditorSubsystem.set_nanite_settings, then post_edit_change
and save. Nanite-off collision meshes (UCX_*) were left alone, correctly.
Result: 111 + 103 = 214 meshes, 0 skipped, 0 still flagged
Wuxianmen already carried 0.0 / 100.0, so it is now the project-wide standard.
Fix 2 — Guidemen V5 4K detail pass
Guidemen is the V5 sibling of Wuxianmen and shares its `_ReferenceTuned` material
family, but never received the revision-2/3 treatment. Its two largest surfaces
were flat: 2,170 stone blocks and 16,248 roof tiles, both uniform.
Stone — 15 components, 1,889 instances
custom data 0 = UV offset 1 = wall height 0..1 2 = tone seed
wall-height stain, per-instance tone 0.72..1.22, restrained moss on the base
Roof tile — 12 components, 16,270 instances
per-instance tone 0.86..1.16 so the roof is not one flat surface
Unlike Wuxianmen these materials also sample an AO map, so the rebuild
replicates that hookup: BaseColor x tint, Normal, MR-G roughness, MR-B metallic, AO-R.
Validation
• Nanite sweep over all seven Blueprints: 228 Nanite meshes checked, 0 offenders. Every one reports error 0.0 and percent 100.0.
• Guidemen: 47 components and 18,822 instances preserved; collision profile, visibility and shadow flags unchanged; every instance transform byte-identical to the pass baseline.
• New materials bound to 15 stone and 12 tile components; custom-data channels sized 3 and 1; wall-height input spans −13 to 1,095 cm.
Limits

No perspective review was possible for this pass either: the deferred high-res screenshot still writes one stale frame per requested view. The Guidemen material values are measured and numerically validated but not visually confirmed. The three V3 builds and Zhengnanmen HighFidelity were audited but not materially retuned — they have had dedicated passes of their own, and their roof orientation is verified correct.
